The Idaho Air National Guard's new $6.5M medical training facility at Gowen Field highlights a critical tension - while military readiness matters, Congress keeps throwing money at "readiness infrastructure" without auditing existing programs. The facility's 10,500 sq ft footprint and ICF walls suggest premium construction costs, yet it primarily serves 1,300 personnel for routine immunizations and dental checks.

Meanwhile, veterans nationwide face 6-month VA wait times and border communities get stripped of resources. Real support for troops means prioritizing frontline needs over redundant facilities that pad contractor profits.

Cut the ceremonial ribbon-cutting - start cutting wasteful line items.

Congressman Simpson, the Idaho Air National Guard Medical Training Facility is exactly the type of strategic investment taxpayers support—directly enhancing military readiness without bureaucratic bloat. But let’s be clear: While this project serves troops, the Pentagon still ranks 12th in efficiency with $1.7B wasted on contracts like GEOGRAPHIC SERVICE PROVIDERS (Securigance, $565M) and MULTI-NETWORK SUPPORT SERVICES.

Real accountability means celebrating wins and torching the $28B in terminated DOD contracts that actually qualify as waste.

Priorities matter—fund troops, not grift.

Hospitals in rural areas will shutter services, and low-income families face impossible compliance hurdles.
